key_grammar.point: to부정사의 부사적 용법 (목적, in order to)
key_grammar.source_sentence: Studies show that people who sit in the front row learn and retain more than others in the audience, partially because those in the front row are more eager to learn, and they show more attention to the speaker in order to avoid being called on.

explanation.text: 'in order to + 동사원형'은 '~하기 위해서'라는 목적을 나타내는 to부정사의 부사적 용법이다.
in order to는 목적을 나타내는 to부정사를 더 분명히 한 형태로, in order to avoid는 '피하기 위해서'로 해석한다.
in order to 뒤에는 반드시 동사원형이 오고, 그 뒤의 avoid는 목적어로 동명사(being called)를 취한다.
부정의 목적(~하지 않기 위해)은 in order not to로 나타낸다.

key_grammar.example_analysis: they show more attention ... in order to avoid being called on에서 in order to avoid가 '지목당함을 피하기 위해'라는 목적을 나타내며 앞 절을 수식한다.

drills.question: 다음 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 적절하지 않은 것은?
drills.sentence: Studies show that people [[1|who]] sit in the front row learn and retain more [[2|than]] others in the audience, partially [[3|because]] those in the front row [[4|are]] more eager to learn, and they show more attention to the speaker in order to avoid [[5|to be called]] on.
drills.fix: avoid는 목적어로 동명사를 취하므로 to be called이 아니라 being called이 되어야 한다(원문: being called).

drills.question: 각 네모 안에서 어법에 맞는 것을 고르시오.
drills.sentence: We found [[that/what]] this strategy not only increased the participation and recall of the normally negative participants [[who/which]] sat up front, it also decreased the participation and recall of the usually positive participants who [[had been sent/had sent]] to the back.
drills.fix: 완전한 절을 이끄는 명사절 접속사 that, 사람 선행사의 주격 관계대명사 who, '보내진'이라는 수동·과거완료의 had been sent가 옳다.

drills.question: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장은?
drills.answer: In one experiment we conducted, we placed name cards on participants' seats so they could not took their usual positions.
drills.fix: 조동사 could 뒤에는 동사원형이 와야 하므로 took이 아니라 take가 되어야 한다(원문: could not take).
options: ① Those in the middle sections are the next most attentive and ask the most questions, as the middle section is considered a safe area, surrounded by others.
② The side areas and back are the least responsive and attentive.
③ In one experiment we conducted, we placed name cards on participants' seats so they could not took their usual positions.
④ We intentionally sat enthusiastic people to the sides and rear of the room, and well-known back-row hermits sat in the front.

⑤ We found that this strategy not only increased the participation and recall of the normally negative participants who sat up front, it also decreased the participation and recall of the usually positive participants who had been sent to the back.

drills.question: 그녀는 시험에 합격하기 위해 매일 밤 열심히 공부했다.
drills.answer: She studied hard every night in order to pass the exam.

drills.question: 측면 구역들과 뒷자리는 가장 반응이 적고 주의도 적다.
drills.answer: The side areas and back are the least responsive and attentive.

misreads.statement: 앞줄에 앉는 사람들은 지목당하는 것을 피하려고 발표자에게 더 많은 주의를 기울인다.
앞줄에 앉은 사람들이 더 많이 배우는 것은 그들이 발표자에게 지목당하기 때문이다.

misreads.why: 지목을 피하려 주의할 뿐, 지목당함 자체가 더 배우는 원인은 아니다.

mistips: in order to + 동사원형 = ~하기 위해서(목적), 뒤의 avoid는 동명사 목적어(being called)를 취한다.
